content.text: No MFN obligation on Customer exists anywhere in the document; § 12.3 expressly disclaims one.

input.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation or price/terms-matching obligation on Customer. Section 12.3 affirmatively confirms that Customer has made no "most-favoured-customer" commitment and leaves Customer free to deal with any supplier or on any terms. The pricing provisions were checked independently: § 7.1 fixes Fees at Order Form levels with no benchmarking or matching mechanic, and § 8.3 caps renewal uplifts (CPI or 3%, whichever is lower) in Customer's favour rather than requiring Customer to extend better third-party terms to Vendor. No disclosure, right-to-match, or best-offer mechanic appears anywhere in the document. This sits at the preferred position (no Customer MFN obligation), so no redline is proposed. Separate burdens found elsewhere (the § 2.2 exclusivity, § 2.1 take-or-pay, and § 12.4 non-compete) are outside this rule's scope and are addressed under their own rules.
